title: Choose which requests remain debuggable
description: Compare expected retained evidence using explicit request classes and sampling probabilities. No vendor prices, maturity scores, or incident-time promises are assumed.

workloads.label: Checkout incident
workloads.detail: Failures are rare enough that uniform sampling can remove most request evidence.

classes.label: Normal
classes.description: Successful requests within the latency objective.

classes.label: Slow
classes.description: Successful requests outside the latency objective.

workloads.label: Rare admin failure
workloads.detail: A low-volume critical path produces very little incident evidence per window.

classes.label: Normal
classes.description: Successful requests within the latency objective.

classes.label: Slow
classes.description: Successful requests outside the latency objective.

workloads.label: Batch pressure
workloads.detail: High volume makes always-on retention expensive in count even when incidents are uncommon.

classes.label: Normal
classes.description: Successful operations within the processing objective.

classes.label: Slow
classes.description: Successful operations outside the processing objective.

policies.label: Always-on
policies.detail: Retain every modeled trace in the window.

policies.label: Parent-based head probability
policies.detail: Apply one probability at the root and preserve that sampled decision across child spans.

policies.label: Tail-priority policy
policies.detail: Retain completed slow and failed traces; sample normal traces at the baseline rate.
